To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Kalman filter is more efficient than the spatial filtering approach in the case of the turbulent flow around a circular cylinder.

the use of the shear-improved SISM (shearing-influenced Smagorinsky) model in a LES simulation of a jet flow in a turbine stage allows to obtain a very good agreement between the computed and experimental mean velocity and turbulence intensity profiles.

a) the SISM model with an adapted spatial filtering method allows to simulate complex turbulent flows, b) the Kalman filter is more robust than the local averaging method, but both methods give similar results for the SISM model, c) the flow control device has a strong impact on the flow in the stator leading edge, d) the flow control has a significant impact on the vortex trajectory in the leading edge, e) the vortex trajectory has a direct influence on the noise generation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an acoustic model for the prediction of the sound generated by a flow in an engine.
the study of unsteady flow in turbomachinery, in particular, in turbomachinery with a stator.
the development of an accurate numerical model of the complex flow in the hub of a gas turbine engine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present work has shown the feasibility of the use of LES in the simulation of the flow field of the stator of a gas turbine engine.

(i) the SISM model is well suited to LES simulations of complex flows, (ii) both methods for computing the filtered velocity field are able to capture the large-scale structures and turbulence intensities in the flow field, (iii) the Kalman filter method is more accurate than the low-pass filter method and is therefore recommended for LES simulations.
the proposed method is a very powerful tool to predict the acoustic behavior of turbomachinery components.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method to extract the mean flow field in LES simulations.

the use of the SISM model with the Kalman filter for the estimation of the mean field, and a LES approach for the simulation of the unsteady part of the flow field, leads to an excellent agreement between experimental data and numerical results in a wide variety of configurations, and that the use of a suction device in the shroud of the blade row is able to reduce the levels of unsteadiness in the flow field, and therefore reduce the acoustic sources in the blade row.

we have been able to obtain a very good agreement between the experimental data and the results of the simulations, with the use of a subgrid model for the large eddy simulation (LES) and a zonal approach (LES in the hub, RANS in the shroud) for the flow around the stator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kalman filter is a very good candidate to extract the mean flow field from the LES data.
a simple and effective way to reduce the sound levels in the jet mixing layer can be achieved by a simple aspiration device.
the Kalman filter is a very promising method for the extraction of a mean flow from large-eddy simulations.
